payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When a new engine uses an older kit with a plain local ledger, every offered engine write form, read and commit hook shall preserve the released 0.45.0 engine's observable reports, events and checks, proven by the extended byte-for-byte comparison.
- When a vault-configured repository lacks a required kit capability, the new engine shall refuse before writing, name the incompatible kit and give the upgrade command; a kit that supplies the required API shall work regardless of its declared version.
- When any inventoried unmodified old engine or old kit runs against the switched repository, it shall read canonically or refuse, and tested prevention shall stop invisible local events even when that process never loads new code; the new kit shall detect such unsafe attempts.
- Before release or live switch, the full old-tool matrix, frozen-ledger at-rest fact, engine-to-kit API audit, failed-check reruns and consumer rehearsal shall pass and the owner shall review the resulting runbook.
payload.description:
## Context
When an installed engine and a repository kit come from different generations, I want existing local-ledger use to remain compatible and switched repositories to prevent invisible local writes, so an upgrade or an older tool cannot bypass the vault.

## Observed failures
Candidate C2 engine still declares 0.45.0. With 373 unchanged v0.45.0 catalog files and exact installed metadata 0.45.0, basicly check exits 0; the released kit creates a local record; candidate basicly tracker write -- comments add RECORD TEXT exits 1: Error: module 'basicly_tracker_kit_vault_write' has no attribute 'admission'. Evidence in codex-vault-cut-c2-land/build/c2-skew-observation.json and .txt; fixture preserved in build/c2-skew-fixture.
Conversely, codex-1 ran an unchanged 0.45.0 wheel engine against the switched scratch repository with candidate kit. tracker write -- comments add dev-j6oqo "Scratch old-tool safety note." exited 0 and appended one local event absent from both vault and queue; config, queue and clone were unchanged. Evidence in development .orchestrator/codex-1-cut-d/old-tool/report.json and engine-comment/. The preceding session/show/list/ready rows passed; later matrix rows were not run.

## Scope and decision
P0 blocks release, global upgrade and live development switch. One owner for the eventual write-entry-point fix: codex-2. No fix tonight. Design waits for codex-1's full old-tool matrix and exact at-rest ledger layout. Inventory all installed tool copies, including unchanged Windows tools, before approving the runbook. A fix only in new engine code cannot stop an old tool that never loads it. Require capability checks rather than version-only guesses. Plain-ledger compatibility must be compared with the released engine across engine-driven forms as well as standalone kit forms; never mix kit generations inside one write. Related basicly-8sgwznb records the same mismatch class despite equal displayed versions.

These intentionally load engine-packaged code, not an older project's missing module. Global basicly_tracker_kit_* module-cache coexistence with project loads still needs generation-consistency tests.
Migration: B's new migrate verb is standalone cli.py -> vault_migration_cli.run; B introduced no engine-source call into that API. Do not infer engine migration support from version text.
Board: tracker_query.board_kit loads PROJECT board/server.py; server/routes load sibling tracker CLI. C2 default_prefix/api_version newly call vault_cli.read_ledger, absent in v0.45.0. A matched older pair makes no new call; partial board/tracker upgrades require coverage.
